title: Tesla (TSLA) Q2 2026 Earnings: Revenue Beat, EPS Miss, Operating Margin Falls to 1.4%
summary: Tesla Q2 2026 revenue of $28.24B beat estimates by 6.84%, but adjusted EPS of $0.33 missed the $0.54 consensus by 38%. Operating margin fell to 1.4% as CapEx surged, while record deliveries of 480,126 vehicles rose 25% year-over-year.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR — Tesla Q2 2026 at a glance:** - **Revenue** of $28.24 billion exceeded the $26.43 billion consensus estimate by 6.84% ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). - **Adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS** of $0.33 missed the $0.54 consensus estimate by 38.35% ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). - **GAAP operating margin** was 1.4%, with operating income of $398 million, down approximately 57% year-over-year ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ;[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ). - The company guided **full-year 2026 capital expenditures to exceed $25 billion** , with further growth over the next two to three years, as stated by CFO Vaibhav Taneja on the July 22, 2026 earnings call ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). - TSLA shares closed at $321.55 on August 5, 2026, with a 52-week range of $297.38–$498.83 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ). --- ## Key Numbers — Tesla Q2 2026 (Quarter Ended June 29, 2026) Metric Actual Consensus Estimate YoY Change vs. Estimate Revenue $28.24B $26.43B +0.50% **Beat** (+6.84%) Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) $0.33 $0.54 — **Miss** (−38.35%) GAAP EPS $0.31 — +5.50% — GAAP Operating Income $398M — −57% (approx.) — GAAP Operating Margin 1.4% — vs. prior-year Q2 — Net Income (GAAP) $1.11B — +18.72% — Free Cash Flow −$1.09B — −127.37% — Q2 Vehicle Deliveries 480,126 — +25% — *Consensus estimates sourced from Google Finance / Nasdaq, dated July 22, 2026. Consensus provider not explicitly named in available materials; figures are third-party estimates. EPS labeled non-GAAP per earnings report presentation. YoY revenue change per CNN data.*
*Sources:*[Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) *,*[CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) *,*[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) *,*[GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) --- ## 1. Did Tesla beat or miss in Q2 2026? ### 1.1 Revenue Tesla reported Q2 2026 total revenue of **$28.24 billion** , exceeding the consensus estimate of **$26.43 billion** by approximately **$1.81 billion** , or **+6.84%** ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). Revenue increased approximately **0.50%** year-over-year, according to CNN financial data ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) ). ### 1.2 Earnings Per Share Tesla reported **adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings per share of $0.33** , which fell below the consensus estimate of **$0.54** by **$0.21** , or **−38.35%** ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). GAAP EPS was **$0.31** , up 5.50% from the prior-year quarter ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) ). ### 1.3 Operating Income and Margins GAAP operating income was **$398 million** , down approximately 57% year-over-year ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). The GAAP operating margin was **1.4%** ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). The net income of $1.11 billion included a $1 billion unrealized gain on Tesla's equity investment in SpaceX, partially offset by approximately $300 million in foreign exchange losses and about $100 million in Bitcoin-related losses, as stated by CFO Vaibhav Taneja on the earnings call ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). --- ## 2. How did TSLA stock react? As of August 5, 2026, Tesla (TSLA) shares closed at **$321.55** ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ). The 52-week range for TSLA is **$297.38 to $498.83** , with the 52-week low reached recently before a rebound ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ;[Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). The company reported Q2 2026 results **after market close on July 22, 2026** ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). Following the earnings release, TSLA shares declined between 3% and 4% in after-hours trading ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). On August 5, 2026, the intraday range was **$320.28 to $327.14** , with trading volume of approximately **27.82 million shares** , below the average daily volume of approximately **47.66 million** ([Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/TSLA/) ). The market capitalization was approximately **$1.29 trillion** ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) ). --- ## 3. What guidance did Tesla give? On the Q2 2026 earnings call held July 22, 2026, Tesla management provided the following forward-looking figures. ### 3.1 Capital Expenditures CFO Vaibhav Taneja stated: **"We continue to expect that CapEx for this year will be more than $25 billion. CapEx will grow for the next two or three years as we expand our Robotaxi fleet, expand our production capacity for Optimus, make investments for semiconductor fab, install solar manufacturing capacity, and AI compute infrastructure, in addition to all the other expansions we'll do for other manufacturing for automotive."** ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ) He further noted that Tesla has secured debt facilities providing **up to $30 billion in borrowing capacity** to help accelerate these investments ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). ### 3.2 Operating Expenses Mr. Taneja stated that operating expenses, largely driven by R&D, are expected to **"continue to grow in 2026 and beyond"** ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). ### 3.3 Free Cash Flow Free cash flow was negative $1.09 billion in Q2 2026 and is expected to remain pressured by elevated capital expenditures ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) ;[Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). ### 3.4 Energy Business Margins CFO Taneja guided that **"long term, we believe the energy business should normalize at a gross margin rate in the mid to low 20% range"** ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). All forward-looking figures above are the company's own statements, made on July 22, 2026, and are subject to risks and uncertainties described in Tesla's SEC filings. The company's forward-looking-statements cautionary language was referenced during the earnings call by Travis Axelrod, Head of Investor Relations. --- ## 4. What did Tesla report by segment? ### 4.1 Segment Performance Tesla achieved **record Q2 vehicle deliveries** of **480,126 units globally** , up approximately 25% year-over-year ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ;[GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). Key segment highlights as disclosed on the earnings call include: - **Automotive gross margins, excluding regulatory credits** , declined sequentially from **19.2% to 16.3%** . CFO Taneja noted that Q1 2026 had a $230 million benefit from warranty true-downs and tariff relief that did not repeat in Q2. Controlling for those items, automotive gross margins excluding credits would have been "approximately flat" quarter-over-quarter ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). - **Energy generation and storage** deployed **13.5 GWh** of energy storage, a 53% sequential increase. Energy gross margins declined from **39.5% to 20.4%** , driven by a $240 million warranty true-up related to vendor cell issues in legacy deployments and the non-repeat of over $200 million in Q1 tariff benefits. Industrial storage average selling prices were also declining amid growing competition ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). - **Services and Other** revenue grew approximately **50% year-over-year** to over **$4.5 billion** , with gross margins reaching an all-time high of **14.1%** , driven by used car sales, paid Supercharging, service centers, and insurance ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ;[GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). - **FSD (Full Self-Driving)** attach rates reached nearly **1.5 million paid customers globally** , with 55% as upfront purchases and 45% as subscriptions. In North America, approximately **55% of Q2 deliveries** had FSD subscription enabled at the time of delivery ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). - **Robotaxi** cumulative unsupervised miles exceeded **380,000** across six cities in two U.S. states, with zero notable safety incidents, as reported by Ashok Elluswamy, VP of AI ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). ### 4.2 Management Commentary **Elon Musk, CEO** , said on the July 22, 2026 earnings call: > "Yeah, it's been a great quarter. We achieved record Q2 deliveries. Model Y, I think it's the best-selling car of any kind in the world and is setting records across the board. Its popularity is increasing tremendously. We're seeing in locations that have FSD approved, we're seeing a very high take rate of FSD. In fact, I think for a lot of people, they're actually buying Tesla Full Self-Driving with a car attached, as opposed to a car with FSD." ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ) **Vaibhav Taneja, CFO** , stated on the same call: > "Q2 continued the trend that we saw at the end of Q1, a resurgence in demand for our vehicles across the globe. We achieved record Q2 deliveries globally with sequential growth across the Americas, APAC and EMEA of 60%, 27% and 12% respectively. Additionally, Model Y set records in several key markets, including the Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand. The efforts of the Tesla team to create compelling products at a reasonable price with the capability of autonomous driving are coming to fruition. We exited Q2 with our largest order backlog since 2023." --- ## 5. What risk factors did Tesla disclose? Tesla's management and SEC filings disclosed the following risk factors relevant to Q2 2026 results. These are drawn from the company's own statements and filings, cited below. ### 5.1 Production Scaling and Supply Chain Constraints CFO Vaibhav Taneja stated that production growth "will be limited by our supply chain. This includes not just batteries, but also electronic components." He noted the company is "working actively to unblock the obstacles ahead by securing strategic deals with suppliers" ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). ### 5.2 Regulatory Investigations The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has opened a formal investigation into over 1 million Model 3 and Model Y vehicles over potential suspension failures ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). ### 5.3 Negative Free Cash Flow and Heavy Capital Investment Cycle Tesla reported negative free cash flow of $1.09 billion in Q2 2026, with CapEx more than doubling sequentially to $5.8 billion ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) ;[Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). CFO Taneja stated that the company expects free cash flow to remain pressured as CapEx increases further in the second half of 2026 and the next two to three years ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). ### 5.4 Autonomous Driving and Robotaxi Regulatory Risk Tesla's VP of AI, Ashok Elluswamy, and other executives discussed the regulatory environment for autonomous vehicles. Lars Moravy, a Tesla executive, noted that "transportation regulatory situations are different city by city, state by state," and that "there's not a federal framework" governing Robotaxi operations. Musk added that any incident, even a single injury, would lead regulators to "immediately clamp down on our activities" ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). ### 5.5 Forward-Looking Statements Cautionary Note During the earnings call, Travis Axelrod, Head of Investor Relations, stated: "During this call, we will discuss our business outlook and make forward-looking statements. These comments are based on our predictions and expectations as of today. Actual events or results could differ materially due to a number of risks and uncertainties, including those mentioned in our most recent filings with the SEC" ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). --- ## 6. When is Tesla's next earnings date? The following calendar dates have been published for Tesla, Inc.: - **Next earnings date (Q3 2026):** **October 21, 2026** , per Yahoo Finance, or **October 27, 2026** , per CNN. Note that October 21 is the date listed by Yahoo Finance; October 27 appears on CNN. Fidelity Investments lists the October date as "unconfirmed" ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ;[CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) ;[Fidelity](https://digital.fidelity.com/prgw/digital/research/quote/dashboard/summary?symbol=TSLA) ). - **Dividend:** Tesla does not currently pay a dividend. The forward dividend and yield and ex-dividend date are listed as "—" ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ;[Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/TSLA/) ). --- ## FAQ **What was Tesla's revenue in Q2 2026?** Tesla reported Q2 2026 total revenue of **$28.24 billion** , exceeding the consensus estimate of **$26.43 billion** by approximately 6.84% ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). **What was Tesla's EPS for Q2 2026?** Tesla reported **adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings per share of $0.33** , which fell below the consensus estimate of $0.54 by 38.35% ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ). GAAP EPS was $0.31 ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/TSLA) ). **What was Tesla's operating margin in Q2 2026?** Tesla's GAAP operating margin was **1.4%** in Q2 2026, with operating income of $398 million ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ;[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ). **How many vehicles did Tesla deliver in Q2 2026?** Tesla achieved a second-quarter delivery record of approximately **480,126 vehicles globally** , up approximately 25% year-over-year ([Google Finance](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/TSLA:NASDAQ) ;[GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). **What is Tesla's CapEx guidance for 2026?** CFO Vaibhav Taneja stated that **full-year 2026 capital expenditures will exceed $25 billion** , with CapEx expected to grow further over the next two to three years ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8973433/tesla-inc-tsla-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-record-deliveries-and-strategic-investments-amid-margin-pressures?mobile=true) ). **What is Tesla's current stock price and 52-week range?** As of August 5, 2026, TSLA shares closed at **$321.55** , with a 52-week range of **$297.38 to $498.83** ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/) ). --- > This article is a factual summary of publicly disclosed financial results, prepared for educational purposes.
